newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn - VAT cuts priority, not income tax.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn - VAT cuts priority, not income tax.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday that the government's longer term aim was to cut the tax burden, but that reductions in Value Added Tax (VAT) were the priority over income tax reductions.

Strauss-Kahn said that if the audit of public finances due on July 21 showed a serious situation concerning the public deficit, this would prove that the previous government's five-year income tax reduction programme had not been supported by the necessary funding.
"That would mean the tax strategy was a strategy which was not funded...We've always said that if there were taxes to be cut, it should be VAT first," he told a news conference.
"I want us to be able in the longer term to cut the tax burden on households," he said.
Strauss-Kahn stressed that the new left-wing government's plan to create 350,000 jobs in the public sector would be financed by a "redployment of job subsidies".
He said that it was by way of pure illustration when he had said in the past that cancelling income tax cuts during 1998 would release enough funds for the job creation programme.
